title: An Eighth 'Transformers' Movie Is in the Works, With Steven Spielberg Helping Lead
summary:
The giant robots are getting ready to roll out again. Paramount Pictures is working on an eighth "Transformers" movie, according to the film news site IndieWire.

The "Transformers" movies are based on Hasbro toys of robots that can change into cars, trucks and other machines. The films have earned about $5.4 billion at movie theaters around the world.

The biggest news is that famous filmmaker Steven Spielberg has joined the project as an executive producer. That means he will help lead the movie's creative direction, along with producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura. Spielberg was also an executive producer on the original "Transformers" films. He signed on after reading the script.

Writer Jason Fuchs is working on a script that aims to return to the spirit of the original movies. The new film will be set in modern times, but details about the story are being kept secret.

Michael Bay, who directed the first five "Transformers" movies, is in early talks to direct again, IndieWire reports. Nothing is final yet. Shia LaBeouf, the star of the first films, will not return. IndieWire says it is too early for news about the rest of the cast.

The movie is one of the first big projects for Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, the Skydance film chiefs, now that a merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery is complete. IndieWire says the two made meeting with Spielberg one of their first goals in August.

Recent movies in the series did not reach the more than $1 billion earned by 2014's "Transformers: Age of Extinction." They include the spinoff "Bumblebee," "Transformers: Rise of the Beasts" and the animated "Transformers One" from 2024. A planned crossover with "G.I. Joe" is not moving forward, IndieWire learned.
why_it_matters: Transformers is one of the biggest movie series of this century, so its next step matters to fans and to the studio's new leaders. It shows how studios try to bring back popular franchises by returning to what audiences first loved.
